target_customer: Independent experience creators and operators such as festivals, venues, tours and attractions that sell tickets and bookings on their own websites
problem: Experience creators had to stitch together ticketing, booking, payment and marketing tools from third-party platforms that took high fees, held payouts until after events and controlled the customer relationship.
business_model: B2B SaaS plus payment processing fees, with later add-ons such as resale and financing
product_category: Experience commerce platform (booking, ticketing, payments, marketing)

founders.name: Ben Simpson
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder and CEO. TechRound interview says the founders ran Rough Hill for about 10 years and started Rise in 2014. Education not found.

founders.name: Lisa Simpson
founders.background_notes: YC page lists her as Founder and Chief Creative Officer. Education not found.

competitors.name: FareHarbor
competitors.what: Reservation system and distribution platform for tours and activities
competitors.traction_then: Claimed more than $50 million revenue in 2017
competitors.funding_then: Reportedly no external funding before Booking Holdings agreed to buy it in April 2018

competitors.name: Rezdy
competitors.what: SaaS booking platform for the tours and activities market
competitors.funding_then: Raised $1.8 million in early 2017 led by Bailador

competitors.name: Peek
competitors.what: Booking and management software for experiences
competitors.funding_then: Reported to have raised $23 million in June 2018 (from a search summary, not opened)

technical_complexity.rationale: Booking, ticketing, payments and website building are standard engineering, but integrating payments and many experience types in one stack was a lot for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Several established booking systems existed and the product is copyable; stickiness comes from operators running their sales and data on the platform.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large players bought booking systems in 2018 but none absorbed Easol, which stayed independent through 2026.

market_need_then: The founders felt the pain directly while running Rise: many separate platforms, high fees and payouts held until after the event. 2018 consolidation in tours and activities software showed buyers valued the category.

branding.domain_note: Operates at easol.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Aspirational creator language such as turning a passion into an empire

branding.brand_signature: Experience Commerce category label and the tagline Shopify for experiences

brand_strength.rationale: Category phrase is memorable but no source shows press or community about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Easol was built by festival operators who knew the pain of fragmented ticketing and payment tools. It raised a seed in 2021, a $25 million Series A led by Tiger Global in December 2021 and a $30 million extension (equity plus debt) in October 2026 alongside an AI agent product. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found, so it appears to be an active independent growth company.
notes: TechCrunch dates the seed to 2020 while Nordic9 dates it to March 2021; March 2021 used. Bokun was bought by TripAdvisor in 2018. The October 2026 extension was reported as $30 million with $20 million equity and $10 million Viola Credit debt per a search summary of the press release; the PR page itself was not opened.
